issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method signature (findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive)) does not match the problem specification and the solution, which both use a single-parameter signature findStockIngredient(String). In the template, other methods in Stock (add and take) call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, which will cause a compilation error and prevents students from following the intended design described in the problem statement and shown in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Stock class to provide the single-parameter method signature: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (matching the UML and solution). Alternatively, add an overload findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the existing two-parameter method to preserve compatibility with the add/take calls.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method taking a single String parameter, but the template Stock implementation provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with a different signature. This mismatch of the same conceptual method name across artifacts (different parameter lists) can confuse students about which method to call/implement and prevents a direct mapping from the problem requirements to the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by adding or replacing a single-parameter method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { ... } (it can delegate to the existing two-parameter version or implement the intended lookup). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to document the two-parameter signature if that was intentional. Prefer adding the single-parameter overload in the template so students can directly follow the spec.
